Fit mvgam models to multiply imputed datasets

Source: R/mvgam_core.R
mvgam_multiple.Rd

Fits one model to each of several imputed datasets and pools the draws, as brms::brm_multiple() does. The pooled posterior holds the uncertainty the imputations add. mvgam(data = ) takes the same list and fits the same models.

Usage

mvgam_multiple(formula, trend_formula = NULL, data_list, combine = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

formula

Main observation model formula (supports brms syntax). Smooth specials s(), t2(), gp(), varying intercepts and slopes, monotonic mo(), measurement-error me(), distributional dpar sub-formulas and offset() are all available. gp() accepts both the approximate Hilbert-space form (gp(x, k = 20)) and the exact full-covariance form (gp(x), no k). Prediction at newdata requires the approximate form. An exact gp() term fits and scores in-sample. mvgam() says so once per session.

trend_formula

A one-sided formula for the latent process: a trend constructor such as AR() with any predictors of the latent state. Write lv_axis() in a term to vary its effect by latent factor, or by series in a model without factors, as in ~ x:lv_axis() + AR(). The series column itself is not supported in a term of this formula. An exact gp() term here also predicts in-sample alone. Forecasting a model that holds one requires the approximate form.

data_list

A list of at least two imputed data frames, or a mids object from mice.

combine

Logical. With imputed data, TRUE (default) pools the imputation fits into one and FALSE returns them as a list.

...

Further arguments to mvgam(), such as family, backend, newdata, chains or iter. Every imputation fit stores newdata.

Value

With combine = TRUE, a pooled fit of class mvgam_pooled, which inherits the class of the imputation fits. Its attribute individual_fits holds those fits. With combine = FALSE, the list of imputation fits. With run_model = FALSE, one unfitted model built from the first dataset. Pooling needs draws, which an unfitted model lacks.

Details

The imputations must hold the same columns, of the same classes, in the same order, with the same number of rows. The columns that place each row on the time and series axes must match exactly. Impute only the response and the covariates.

rstan::sflist2stanfit() concatenates the chains of every imputation fit. The pooled draws then hold both the within- and the between-imputation variance. Because chains from different imputations sample different posteriors, the R-hat of the pooled chains measures disagreement between imputations. summary() reports each parameter's largest R-hat and summed ESS over the imputation fits. It also tabulates the convergence of each fit.

See also

mvgam(), summary.mvgam_pooled()

Other model fitting: check_newdata(), jsdgam(), mvgam(), mvgam_data(), mvgam_formula(), pivot_detection_array(), pivot_species_matrix(), series_to_mvgam(), stancode.mvgam_formula(), update.mvgam()

Examples

# \dontrun{
# A covariate with ten missing values, filled three ways. An
# imputation model would draw the fills. This example draws them
# from a normal distribution.
set.seed(1)
dat <- sim_mvgam(family = gaussian(), n_series = 1L,
                 n_timepoints = 60L, trend_model = AR())$data_train
missing_x <- sample(nrow(dat), 10L)
dat$x[missing_x] <- NA
imputed_list <- lapply(1:3, function(i) {
  filled <- dat
  filled$x[missing_x] <- rnorm(10L, mean(dat$x, na.rm = TRUE),
                               sd(dat$x, na.rm = TRUE))
  filled
})

# One fit per imputation, with the posteriors pooled
fit_pooled <- mvgam_multiple(
  formula = y ~ x,
  trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),
  data_list = imputed_list,
  family = gaussian(),
  chains = 2,
  silent = 2
)
#> Warning: 47 of 2000 (2.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
#> Warning: 220 of 2000 (11.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
#> Warning: 1 of 2 chains had an E-BFMI less than 0.3.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
#> Warning: 110 of 2000 (6.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.

# The summary adds the convergence of each imputation fit
summary(fit_pooled)
